A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GMValuator. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures. Retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v7 reports original class-matching, attribute-matching, noisy-data detection, runtime and sensitivity experiments across several datasets and generative models.

after.justification: v8 retains those empirical results and adds ImageNet and Naruto evaluations, component ablations, and retrieval and scalability experiments.

M1.justification: The operational pipeline retains encoder/PQ recall, perceptual re-ranking, MANIQA calibration, zero contributions outside the selected candidates, and contribution summation. Specifying CLIP and testing alternative encoders does not establish an algorithm change: v7 already allowed pretrained encoders and mentioned VGG-16 only as an example.

E1.justification: v8 adds ImageNet class-matching evaluation and Naruto text-conditioned image generation, substantially broadening the represented image categories and generation tasks. Appendix E.2 also adds simultaneous matching of multiple CelebA attributes. AFHQ and FFHQ evaluations were already present in v7.

E2.justification: Appendix P adds an evaluated exhaustive nearest-neighbor comparator for PQ recall, comparing accuracy and runtime. VAE-TracIn and IF4GAN remain the external baselines in their corresponding original experiments; neither is newly evaluated on ImageNet.

E3.justification: New protocols include ImageNet evaluation with a Masked Diffusion Transformer, Naruto evaluation with LoRA-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion and k=3,4,5, and joint-attribute matching. Appendices O and P introduce fixed-recall scaling tests and a recall-count sweep from 100 to 700. These are added experimental designs, rather than demonstrated reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v8 adds encoder sensitivity tests using CLIP, AlexNet and DenseNet; calibration ablations, including low-quality generated outputs; runtime scaling analyses; and PQ-versus-exhaustive-retrieval tests. These directly examine component necessity and approximation effects. The generated-sample-count sensitivity study from v7 Appendix C is retained in v8 Appendix F.

E5.justification: The original t-tests and 0.01 significance threshold are retained, as are the ten-run sample-size study and its stated mean/standard-deviation reporting. The additions disclose no new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. New score/rank boxplots describe sample distributions rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: The matched older numerical tables are retained, while v8 adds substantial results: ImageNet DreamSim accuracy is 77.27% at k=30, and new tables report joint-attribute, encoder and Naruto outcomes. Appendix P reports 0.25 seconds for PQ attribution versus 13.75 seconds for nearest-neighbor search. Table 6 also reverses the expected v1/v2 ordering in its caption despite retaining the original means and test statistics.

T1.justification: v7 provides a similarity-based motivation without a contributor-recovery theorem. v8 introduces attribute-space and optimal-contributor definitions, Lipschitz assumptions, Theorem 2.4 bounding attribute-classification loss through Wasserstein distances, and a coupling-based proof in Appendix M. This is a substantial theoretical addition, irrespective of the proof's correctness.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement narrow the claimed first model-agnostic, training-free valuation approach from generative models generally to image generation. The central similarity-matching, quality-calibration, efficiency and four-evaluation-criteria contributions remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v8 adds explanations that image-based re-ranking tolerates noisy recall embeddings and that fixed recall counts make re-ranking dominate runtime as datasets grow. It discusses calibration failures with low-quality outputs, explains restrictions on baseline comparisons, and explicitly states the vision-only applicability limitation and proposed NLP extension.

D1.justification: v8 adds a GMValuator code-access link, explicitly identifies CLIP as the experimental encoder, and documents LoRA fine-tuning, RTX A6000 hardware and recall budgets for new experiments. Table 1 corrects the swapped CPU/GPU labels. Existing architecture descriptions largely remain unchanged; the additions do not provide comprehensive training hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The main related-work taxonomy and existing references are retained. v8 adds targeted positioning against Boopathy et al.'s generalization-difficulty measure and explicitly builds its theoretical argument on LAVA, replacing v7's practical-versus-theoretical contrast. Additional citations support the new datasets, encoder, generator and optimal-transport reasoning.

P1.justification: Detailed related work and pseudocode move to appendices; motivation separates theoretical justification from empirical validation; and experimental setup and metrics become distinct subsections. v8 adds a contents list, notation guide and appendix roadmap, alongside language and author-information edits. C3 is renamed from data cleaning to out-of-distribution detection while retaining its original main experiment.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to the single-column ICLR layout. Figure 2 is redrawn, major result tables are reorganized horizontally, the architecture table is split, and Figure 7's retained panels are rearranged. New tables and Figures 8–12 display the added experiments and analyses.

improvement.justification: The new calibration, encoder and retrieval ablations, broader evaluations, and code-access information strengthen the empirical support beyond v7. However, the added theoretical guarantee is not established as written: Appendix M drops a factor of two and uses predictor smoothness absent from Assumption 2.3. Reporting errors, including Table 6's newly reversed caption, further limit the net improvement.
